safety_line: Bites itch and can trigger flea allergy dermatitis in pets. See a doctor if bites become infected or you develop a rash that spreads.
traits: Pets scratching, plus bites appearing around human ankles
Reddish-brown to black, wingless, 1-3 mm, strong jumping legs
Black specks on pet bedding that turn red when wetted ("flea dirt")
Tiny jumpers in carpet, especially in shaded rooms

look_alikes.difference: Cat fleas are visible jumpers on pets and carpet; chiggers are picked up outdoors and too small to see, causing welts at sock lines.
look_alikes.next_photo: A photo of the bites alone can't tell these apart. From a safe distance, note where you were bitten (pets/carpet vs. outdoor plants); a technician judges from that.

copy.what_it_means: Adults on the pet are usually a small share of the infestation — most of it is eggs, larvae and pupae hiding in carpet, bedding and shaded outdoor spots. Treating the pet alone often leaves that reservoir behind; a technician looks at pet, home and yard together and times the approach to the flea life cycle.
copy.fact: Adults on the pet are roughly 5% of the infestation — the other 95% is eggs, larvae, and pupae in carpet and bedding.
copy.blurb: Treating just the pet often isn't enough — the home and yard usually need attention too, timed to the flea life cycle.

tech_notes: IGR + adulticide inside/out; customer prep sheet mandatory (vacuum, wash bedding, pet treatment same week).
